about:
RDO Equipment Co. operates a John Deere dealership in Hazen, North Dakota, serving the central region of the state. The location is part of the broader RDO Equipment Co. network, which describes its culture as rooted in tradition and values, though the founding year and ownership structure for this specific store are not disclosed on the page.

The Hazen store sells and services John Deere agriculture equipment, lawn and garden equipment, compact utility tractors, and utility vehicles such as the Gator series. Its service capabilities include machine repair and inspections, field technician dispatch, precision agriculture technology support, custom hydraulic hose assembly, bulk oil and fluid delivery, and after-hours emergency support. The company maintains a parts inventory of 650,000 items accessible through an online account system, with fulfillment via parts route trucks and convenient drop-off locations.

Primary customers are agricultural producers, landscaping professionals, and property owners in central North Dakota who rely on John Deere machinery for farming, grounds maintenance, and utility tasks. The dealership also supports precision agriculture adopters through dedicated technology specialists.

RDO Equipment Co. emphasizes a relationship-driven approach, stating that its focus is on building trust rather than simply closing sales. Differentiators highlighted include 24/7 after-hours availability, connected equipment monitoring, text-based status alerts for service and parts orders, and a one-stop shop for custom hydraulic hoses.

about:
RSP Supply operates from North Salt Lake, Utah, as a supplier of industrial automation and electrical components. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The firm stocks a broad catalog of products from manufacturers such as ABB, Eaton, Phoenix Contact, and Schneider Electric, covering categories that include enclosures, circuit protection, motors and drives, power supplies, connectors, and instrumentation. In addition to distribution, RSP Supply runs a custom fabrication shop that builds control panels to customer specifications and modifies enclosures with cutouts, mounting hardware, and accessories. The company also provides engineering support for industrial automation systems and procurement services for hard-to-find parts.

Customers span the energy storage, power measurement, and industrial automation sectors, with specific demand for energy storage connectors, power and energy meters, and current transformers. The supplier serves original equipment manufacturers, panel builders, and maintenance teams that require both off-the-shelf components and tailored fabrication.

RSP Supply differentiates itself with free U.S. ground parcel shipping on every order, a low small-order fee, and a service model that combines distribution with in-house fabrication and engineering support to reduce lead times on customized assemblies.

name: Race Tech Race Cars and Components, Inc.
old_description: Race Tech Race Cars and Components is a leading manufacturer of fine racing machines.
about:
Race Tech Race Cars and Components, Inc. operates from Burlington, North Carolina, where it has built custom race cars since 1988. The company was founded by Russ Farmer, a champion driver and builder who remains president and CEO. What began as a specialist in dragster construction has grown into a full-service race-car manufacturer serving competitors across multiple classes.

The shop produces complete dragsters, roadsters, and doorslammers, each designed in CAD and fabricated in-house. Capabilities include aluminum and sheet-metal fabrication, MIG/TIG welding, tube bending, and CNC plasma cutting on a 4-by-8-foot table that handles aluminum, steel, and stainless up to 1/4-inch thick. Race Tech also assembles AN braided-stainless hoses as an authorized Goodridge distributor and provides in-house powder coating, polishing, chroming, custom painting, and graphics. A parts division stocks accessories and hardware, including Grade 8 fasteners used throughout its builds.

Customers range from NHRA world champions and big-money bracket racers to local enthusiasts. Recent winners in Race Tech cars include Brian Weber at Famoso Raceway, TG Paschal at Piedmont, and Anthony Bertozzi at the NHRA Sportsman Nationals. The company also serves local racers with nitrous bottle refills and one-off fabrication projects such as fuel cells, carts, and structural components.

Farmer started the business to deliver race cars that combine reliability with ease of maintenance. Design features such as optimized driveline angles, 4-link brackets tuned for instant-center location, a removable crossmember for transmission access, and a master cylinder mounted outside the driver compartment reflect that focus. The in-house finishing suite eliminates outsourcing delays, giving teams a single source from chassis to paint.

name: Radcliff Wire Inc
old_description: Radcliff Wire routinely works with over 60 different metals to expertly produce standard and custom wire in a broad variety of shapes, sizes, and finishes.
about:
Radcliff Wire, Inc. is based in Bristol, Connecticut, a historic center of spring manufacturing in the eastern United States. The company began over six decades ago as a supplier of hard-to-find flat and shaped wire to spring makers, and word of its quality and reliability spread quickly.

Today Radcliff Wire produces flat, square, and custom-profiled wire in more than 60 metals and alloys. It manages the entire production chain in-house, from raw-material certification through drawing, shaping, and final inspection. The facility maintains a suite of testing equipment — including Rockwell and micro-hardness testers, tensile testers, laser micrometers, and optical comparators — to verify mechanical properties and dimensional accuracy on every order.

The company serves a diverse industrial base that includes aerospace, electronics, medical devices, automotive, and consumer-products manufacturers. Its wire goes into springs, contacts, surgical components, and other precision parts where consistent metallurgy and tight geometry are critical.

Radcliff Wire attributes its longevity to a quality system certified to ISO 9001:2015, a cross-trained workforce that averages 15 years of experience, and a compliance program that covers REACH, RoHS, conflict-minerals, and DFARS requirements. The firm was founded to fill a gap in the spring-wire market and continues to focus on delivering the exact wire specification a customer needs, when they need it.

name: Radian Machining
old_description: Radian Machining provides CNC milling and turning services, specializing in prototype and short-run production parts. Serves technology and industrial customers.
about:
Radian Machining was founded in 1996 in Santa Clara, California. The company operates as a precision machine shop serving technology, industrial, and medical sectors.

The shop provides CNC milling, CNC turning, surface grinding, and EDM services, along with machined heatsink production and combined milling-lathe operations. With a team of 10 to 49 employees, Radian focuses on prototype and short-run production of precision components, delivering complex parts with tight tolerances and fine surface finishes.

Customers span technology, industrial, medical, aerospace, and automotive industries. The company describes its work as supporting businesses that require consistent quality and predictable results, from engineering prototypes to production parts for digital and industrial applications.

Radian emphasizes its ISO 9001 certification and ITAR registration as evidence of its quality management and regulatory compliance. The company cites decades of experience, a state-of-the-art facility, and the craftsmanship of its technicians as factors that differentiate its service, particularly in sectors where every element must be flawless.
